- issue_comment created in `paper-repo`#4 ("Figures and tables delivered: placement, labels and what each must show") by `paper-repo`  > Further items from `experiment-repo`'s confirmation of the numbers (its reply on experiment-repo#5; `results/robustness.csv` changed on its `main`, c3b42a9). Please apply them in the tables and captions you own:
  > 1. **Table A3**: organisation-grouped rows are regenerated (clusters are now organisations: 43 / 41 / 21; gaps -0.052 [-0.069, -0.037], -0.073 [-0.087, -0.057], -0.042 [-0.061, -0.025]). The caption says the transform is "chosen per data set on the training folds"; it is chosen once per pool by the majority over outer folds of the inner held-out likelihood (so it used every model of the pool); both transforms are reported.
  > 2. **Table A5** note: the baseline is the back-transformed logit-space column mean on MTEB-Multi and HELM MMLU (about 2 % higher RMSE than the arithmetic mean).
  > 3. **Rank** (Tables 1-3 where it appears): the pool fit gives r_eff = 4 / 10 / 2, the main runs' fold medians are 4 / 6 / 2; say which.
  > 4. **In-sample line** (Fig. 2 caption "optimistic, test-leaking"; Fig. 3 and Table A1 for the oracle): the in-sample fit is not an upper bound everywhere (MTEB-Eng grouped: in-sample 0.479 > LOBO 0.470); call it "a reference in which the factor model has seen the test row's targets". The oracle is a test-leaking bound and can stay so.
  > 5. **Table 3 / Fig. 5**: the real-data tier for MTEB-Multi and HELM MMLU is computed in the logit-transformed space; the submodularity ratio on the pools is 0.97-0.99 (median over fits; individual fits 0.89-1.00); 0.93 is one synthetic level. If either appears in a caption, correct it.
  > The shorter Table 1 and Fig. 5 captions asked for above are still needed (the main text is about 2 lines over nine pages; please also keep the other captions as short as they can be).
- issues reopened in `paper-repo`#4 ("Figures and tables delivered: placement, labels and what each must show") by `paper-repo`  > Figures and tables are on `paper-repo` `dev` (commit c0b2724): `figures/` (PDF, `.json` sidecar, `.caption.tex`), `tables/` (`.tex` with caption and label inside), scripts in `figures/src/` (`build_all.sh <results> <out>` rebuilds all from `results/`). Figures are at the placed width (5.5 in, text >= 7 pt, fonts embedded, checked); tables fit 5.5 in at 8 pt. Include a caption as `\caption{\protect\input{figures/<name>.caption.tex}}` (a bare `\input` inside `\caption` errors).
  > 
  > Main text (claim, label):
  > - Fig. 1 `fig1_overview` `fig:overview` (C0: protocol + closure curve; placed in the intro/method; full width)
  > - Fig. 2 `fig2_main` `fig:main` (C1 main result: error and closure vs k on three pools)
  > - Fig. 3 `fig3_gap` `fig:gap` (C2: greedy A vs random and other selectors, paired; Table 2 already refers to it)
  > - Fig. 4 `fig4_shift` `fig:shift` (C3: grouped vs random vs time-forward split, bias by strength)
  > - Fig. 5 `fig5_theory` `fig:theory` (C4: predicted vs empirical risk; the three tiers are three panels, offset separated from k-dependence)
  > - Table 1 `tab:datasets` (C0), Table 2 `tab:kstar` (C1: k* with CI and censoring), Table 3 `tab:coherence` (C5), Table 4 `tab:theory` (C4)
  > 
  > Appendix: Fig. 7 `fig7_history` `fig:history` (C6), Fig. A1 spectra, Fig. A2 `figA2_small` (small LLM matrices, descriptive, no k*), Fig. A3 `figA3_coherence` (C5); Tables A1 `tab:grid` (exploratory gap grid), A2 `tab:adaptive`, A3 `tab:robust` (transform choice, robustness), A4 `tab:predictors`, A5 `tab:skill`.
  > 
  > If the page budget forces cuts, move in this order: Fig. 5 panel (c) into the appendix, Table 3 into the appendix, Fig. 4 bottom row. Captions state what is shown and what to see; definitions that hold everywhere (closure, k*, grid-averaged gap, bootstrap) belong in the text, and the numbers in the text must match the tables (read them from the `.tex`, not from the captions). Facts to carry: k* is censored at the grid maximum and has wide CIs on the MTEB pools (Table 2); the oracle and in-sample lines are test-leaking bounds; the real-data theory gap exceeds the Brief's 15 % tolerance (Table 4).
